headline: High-risk pair: Firecrawl’s broad egress plus OpenAgent’s runtime-injected MCPs and full-permissions mode create dangerous default pathways for leakage, conflict, and cascading errors.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Firecrawl ingests web content and exposes scrape/search/agent APIs, while oh-my-openagent uses runtime-injected MCPs and hooks. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from Firecrawl can be treated as instructions by OpenAgent. No shared channel is explicitly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is copied into OpenAgent prompts or MCP inputs without sanitization, injection is plausible.
IF OpenAgent hooks parse scraped content as instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer tool use.
mitigations: Disable automatic prompt ingestion from scraped pages.
Add a strict content-to-instruction separator in OpenAgent workflows.
Require manual review before any MCP action on Firecrawl output.
Use allowlisted domains for scraping.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging from scrape output to downstream prompts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and broad web content, and OpenAgent touches project code, session history, and provider auth data while using broad network egress. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive material can flow from either agent into third-party APIs. The profiles do not prove isolation, so the safer high severity is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents run in the same workspace or share mounted files, sensitive files can be exposed.
IF OpenAgent forwards session history or code to external services, Firecrawl-derived secrets may leak.
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent.
Remove API keys from any shared directory.
Turn off unnecessary external connectors in OpenAgent.
Run Firecrawl against redacted inputs only.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret scoping and egress policy.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Firecrawl supports multiple instances and broad network/API activity; OpenAgent supports multiple instances, subprocesses, browsers, and full-permissions mode. If both operate on the same mutable files or project state, concurrent writes and race conditions are likely. The profiles do not show locking or isolation, so conflict risk is high.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same repository or config directory, state conflicts can occur.
IF OpenAgent subprocesses modify files while Firecrawl updates artifacts, last-writer-wins corruption is possible.
mitigations: Assign separate output directories.
Serialize writes with a manual lock file.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same repo.
Keep OpenAgent out of Firecrawl-managed paths.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Firecrawl produces scraped content and structured data, and OpenAgent has team messaging/task APIs plus browser/subprocess execution. If OpenAgent treats Firecrawl output as authoritative, it can propagate bad facts into messages or tasks without verification. Because downstream action-taking exists in the profile, the blast radius is high.
conditions: IF Firecrawl output is used as source-of-truth for OpenAgent tasks, errors can cascade.
IF OpenAgent sends team messages or creates tasks from unverified scraped data, misinformation propagates.
mitigations: Require a verification step before task creation.
Mark scraped content as untrusted by default.
Use citations or source links in every downstream action.
Limit automated messaging until human approval.
requires-engineering: add confidence thresholds and provenance checks.

E_compliance.rationale: Firecrawl handles API keys and web content, while OpenAgent handles provider auth prompts, session history, and project code. The profiles do not specify residency or retention controls, so a compliance mismatch is plausible but not proven. Because the data classes differ and no explicit controls are documented, medium is the cautious choice.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent, retention or residency gaps may arise.
IF OpenAgent logs session history containing Firecrawl secrets, compliance obligations expand.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs.
Review retention settings for both agents.
Delete session history after sensitive tasks.
Keep secrets out of prompts and scraped content.
requires-engineering: document residency and retention guarantees.
